Page iv
Introduction
The following document is the specification of the REST API TMF687 for Stock Management.
It includes the model definition as well as all available operations.
This API features several resources:
•
StockLevel
describes a stock of a StockItem. It includes quantity information (in stock,
min, max, reorder) as well as place and related party references. This replaces the v4
ProductStock resource.
•
AdjustStockLevel
is
a
task
resource
used
to
request
a
stock
level
quantity
adjustment.
A
reason
for
adjustment
may
be
provided
(for
example,
insufficient
inventory).
•
CheckStockLevel
is a
task resource
used to check StockItem availability at a place
and
date.
The
server
may
provide
alternate
options
when
the
requested
item
is
not
available.
•
QueryStockLevel
is
a
task
resource
used
to
retrieve
a
list
of
stock
levels
matching
complex
search
criteria
(for
example,
stock
levels
in
a
given
state,
at
a
place,
and
available for a channel).
•
ReserveStockLevel
is a
task resource
used to perform a reservation for a StockItem.
The requester may specify a stock level to use. A related entity may link the reservation
to another entity (such as a product order or quote).
•
CancelReserveStockLevel
is a
task resource
used to trigger cancellation of a reserve
stock level task and to provide cancellation information (timestamp and reason).
Stock Management API performs the following operations
…on StockLevel:
•
Retrieval of a stock level or a collection of stock levels depending on filter criteria
•
Partial update of a stock level (including updating rules)
•
Creation of a stock level
•
Deletion of stock level (for administration purposes)
•
Notification of events on stock level
◦
stock level creation
◦
stock level deletion
◦
stock level attribute value change

stock level state change

The
batch
notification
(

not
one
of

CancelReserveStockLevel cancellation reason
cancellationReason
is
mandatory
on
CancelReserveStockLevel
.
Callers
must
supply the reason when creating the cancel task; there is no separate informationRequired
notification for this API.
…on
AdjustStockLevel,
CheckStockLevel,
QueryStockLevel,
ReserveStockLevel
and
CancelReserveStockLevel:
•
Retrieval of a task resource depending on filter criteria – or by id
•
Creation of a task resource
•
Notification of events
◦
for creation
◦
for state change
StockLevel status and usage type
StockLevel is a managed entity. Its
status
attribute describes whether the quantity can be
allocated.
Its
usageType
attribute
describes
the
operational
inventory
category
(for
example, stock in the shop versus stock in transit). Implementations must interpret both
attributes together.
status
is
a
closed
enumeration
(
StockLevelStatusType
).
usageType
is
an
extensible
string (
StockLevelUsageType
): the values listed below are typical, and implementations
may define additional values.
Status values
Stock Management User Guide
© TM Forum 2026. All Rights Reserved.
Page 2
Status
When to use
available
The quantity can be allocated or sold (for example, sellable stock of
Galaxy S22 Ultra ready in the Lyon shop).
reserved
The quantity is held for a specific purpose (for example, a product
order or quote) and must not be reallocated to another requester
until the reservation is completed or cancelled.
unavailable
The quantity cannot be allocated (for example, damaged handsets
awaiting write-off, or stock under quarantine).
unknown
The inventory status has not yet been determined (for example,
newly created StockLevel before the first stock count).

Value
Meaning (illustrative)
inShop
Quantity held in a retail shop (back store and/or sales floor),
distinct from web-channel-only views.
onDisplay

Quantity returned for inspection or restocking; often
unavailable
until accepted back into sellable stock.

paired with status
unavailable
.
Link between status and usageType
•
status
answers: “Can this quantity be allocated now?”
Stock Management User Guide
© TM Forum 2026. All Rights Reserved.
Page 4
•
usageType
answers: “What operational category is this quantity in?”
They are complementary, not substitutes. Examples:
•
Lyon shop sellable handsets:
status=available
,
usageType=inShop
•
Handsets reserved for product order PO-123:
status=reserved
,
usageType=inShop
•
Damaged display units:
status=unavailable
,
usageType=damaged
•
Shipment to Lyon not yet received:
status=unavailable
,
usageType=inTransit
•
Returns awaiting inspection:
status=unavailable
,
usageType=returned
•
New StockLevel before first count:
status=unknown
,
usageType
may already be set
(for example
inShop
) when the intended category is known
State change notifications for StockLevel should report the changed
status
. Usage-type
changes are attribute value changes when only that field is updated.
QueryStockLevel and searchCriteria
QueryStockLevel
is a task resource used to find matching
StockLevel
resources. Prefer
GET
/stockLevel
with filter (or JSONPath) for simple lookups of known stock levels. Use
QueryStockLevel
when you need:
•
multi-criteria template matching via
searchCriteria
•
optional
asynchronous
completion
(
instantSyncCheck
set
to
false)
with
task
state
and notifications
•
parity with the other stock task resources (Check, Reserve, Adjust)
How searchCriteria works
searchCriteria
is
an
array
of
StockLevel
templates.
Each
template
lists
only
the
attributes that should constrain the search.
•
Within one template: supplied attributes are combined with AND (all must match).
•
Across templates: each array entry is evaluated independently (OR). A StockLevel that
matches any template is returned.
•
Omit attributes that must not constrain the search. Unspecified fields are ignored as
filters.
•
On create, do not send server-managed fields (
id
,
href
,
creationDate
,
lastUpdate

Task resource item state aggregation
For
multi-item
task
resources
(
AdjustStockLevel
,
CheckStockLevel
,
ReserveStockLevel
),
each
item
may
carry
its
own
state
.
The
parent
task
state
is
consolidated as follows:
•
If any item is
terminatedWithError
(or failed), the task is
terminatedWithError
/
failed.
•
Else if any item is
inProgress
or
acknowledged
while others are not yet complete, the
task is
inProgress
.
•
Else if all items are
done
, the task is
done
.
Partial failure is allowed: successful items are
done
and failed items remain in an error state,
with the parent task in an error/failed state.
Task resource lifecycle
The
state
machine
specifying
the
typical
state
change
transitions
for
task
resources
is
provided below. This is standard task resource lifecycle:
Stock Management User Guide
© TM Forum 2026. All Rights Reserved.
Page 8
State
Definition
Acknowledged
The acknowledged state is where a task
request has been received and has passed
message and basic business validations.
InProgress
The In Progress state is when the task
request is being processed by the stock
management system.
TerminatedWithErrors
The task request could not be completed
successfully. Task result is not available.
Done
The task request has been assessed and
result available.
Major changes from v4 to v5
The
main

TMF687

is

item
Stock Management User Guide

being stocked, and the replacement of the
ProductStock
managed entity with
StockLevel
.
StockLevel describes inventory for a StockItem at a place (and optionally channel), rather
than tying stock directly to a Product configuration. Task resources (Check, Query, Reserve,
Cancel Reserve, and Adjust) operate on stock levels and stock items using this model.

SAMPLE USE CASES
We illustrate in this document several use cases:
•
For StockLevel we illustrate a description of a stock item of “Galaxy S22 Ultra” in shop &
available
in
the
Lyon
shop.
We
have
all
information
related
to
this
stock
as
min/max/reorder quantity or next replenishment date.
•
For adjust StockLevel we request to change previous stock level quantity following an
inventory check.
•
For check, a requester asks for a 128GB Galaxy S22 Ultra availability in the Lyon shop.
This
item
is
not
available
but
an
alternate
is
available:
a
256GB
Galaxy
S22
Ultra.
Because request is ok to get alternate this proposal is sent in the response.
•
For reserve StockLevel, we reserve this 256GB Galaxy S22 Ultra in the Lyon shop. The
product order related to this reservation is part of the resource information.
•
For query StockLevel we look for Galaxy S22 Ultra available in a defined search zone. In
the response we have 2 shops listed with this stock item.
See

and
searchCriteria
in

Introduction
for
how

templates work (AND within a template, OR across templates), which attributes are typical
filters, and JSON examples.

Support of polymorphism and extension
Support of polymorphic collections and types and schema based extension is provided by
means
of
a
list
of
generic
meta-attributes
that
we
describe
below.
Polymorphism
in
collections occurs when entities inherit from base entities, for instance a specialized stock
level type inheriting properties from the base StockLevel entity.
Generic
support
of
polymorphism
and
pattern
extensions
is
described
in
the
TMF
API
Guidelines v3.0 Part 2 document.
The
@type
attribute
provides
a
way
to
represent
the
actual
class
type
of
an
entity.
For
example,
within
a
list
of
StockLevel
instances
some
may
be
specialized
subtypes
of
StockLevel. The @type gives this information. All resources and sub-resources of this API
have a @type attributes that can be provided when this is useful.
The
@referredType
can
be
used
within
reference
entities
(for
example
StockLevelRef,
PlaceRef,
ChannelRef,
or
ProductSpecificationRef)
to
explicitly
denote
the
actual
entity
type of the referred class. Notice that in reference entities the @type, when used, denotes
the class type of the reference itself, such as StockLevelRef, and not the class type of the
referred object. However since reference classes are rarely sub-classed, @type is generally
not useful in reference objects.
The @schemaLocation property can be used in resources to allow specifying user-defined
properties of an Entity or to specify the expected
characteristics
of an entity.
The
@baseType
attribute
gives
a
way
to
provide
explicitly
the
base
of
class
of
a
given
resource that has been extended

Resources are physical or non-physical components (or some combination of these) within
an
enterprise’s
infrastructure
or
inventory.
They
are
typically
consumed
or
used
by
services (for example a physical port assigned to a service) or contribute to the realization
of a Product (for example, a SIM card). They can be drawn from the Application, Computing
and Network domains, and include, for example, Network Elements, software, IT systems,
content
and
information,
and
technology
components.
A
ResourceSpecification
is
an
abstract base class for representing a generic means for implementing a particular type of
Resource.
In
essence,
a
ResourceSpecification
defines
the
common
attributes
and
relationships of a set of related Resources, while Resource defines a specific instance that
is based on a particular ResourceSpecification.

ResourceSpecificationRef sub-resource fields
Resources are physical or non-physical components (or some combination of these) within
an
enterprise’s
infrastructure
or
inventory.
They
are
typically
consumed
or
used
by
services (for example a physical port assigned to a service) or contribute to the realization
of a Product (for example, a SIM card). They can be drawn from the Application, Computing
and Network domains, and include, for example, Network Elements, software, IT systems,
content
and
information,
and
technology
components.
A
ResourceSpecification
is
an
abstract base class for representing a generic means for implementing a particular type of
Resource.
In
essence,
a
ResourceSpecification
defines
the
common
attributes
and
relationships of a set of related Resources, while Resource defines a specific instance that
is based on a particular ResourceSpecification.
See
[ResourceSpecificationRef]
for details.

StockLevel sub-resource fields
Represents the inventory level of a specific stock item at a particular location, including its
quantity, availability status and related inventory management information.
alertThreshold
A Quantity. An amount in a given unit.
channel
A ChannelRef [0..*]. Sales or distribution channel(s) for
which this stock level applies (for example retail shop or
web channel).
creationDate
A DateTime. Date when the StockLevel was created
(whatever its status).
description
A String. Additional information describing the stock level
and its intended usage.
href
A String. Hyperlink reference.
id
A String. Unique identifier.
lastInventoryDate
A DateTime. Last inventory count date for this StockLevel.
lastUpdate
A DateTime. Last date when the StockLevel record was
updated.
maxQuantity
A Quantity. An amount in a given unit.
minQuantity
A Quantity. An amount in a given unit.
name
A String [1]. Human-readable name assigned to the stock
level.
place
A PlaceRef. A reference to a physical Place.
productSpecification
A ProductSpecificationRef. ProductSpecification
reference. A product Specification represents entities
that are orderable from the provider of the catalog.
quantity
A Quantity [1]. An amount in a given unit.
relatedParty
A RelatedPartyRefOrPartyRoleRef [0..
]. A list of related
party references (RelatedParty [
]). A related party
defines party or party role linked to a specific entity.
reorderQuantity
A Quantity. An amount in a given unit.
replenishmentDate
A DateTime. Planned date for future replenishment for this
StockLevel.
Stock Management User Guide
© TM Forum 2026. All Rights Reserved.
Page 35
status
A StockLevelStatusType [1]. Availability status of the stock
represented by a StockLevel. Use available when the
quantity can be allocated or sold; reserved when the
quantity is held for a specific purpose (for example a
product order or quote) and must not be reallocated;
unavailable when the quantity cannot be allocated (for
example damaged, quarantined, or otherwise not ready for
use); unknown when the inventory status has not yet been
determined (for example before the first stock count).
ENUMERATED with values:
* reserved
* available
* unavailable
* unknown
stockItem
A StockItem [1]. Identification of the stock item used by
the logistics system.
usageType
A StockLevelUsageType. Operational inventory category
of the StockLevel. This is an extensible string (not a closed
enumeration); implementations may define additional
values. Typical values: inTransit (quantity currently being
shipped between locations); onDisplay (quantity on a
retail storefront display); damaged (quantity that cannot
be sold until repaired, written off, or otherwise cleared);
returned (quantity returned for inspection or restocking);
replenishmentInProgress (additional quantity is expected
soon); inShop (quantity held in a retail shop location,
typically back-of-store or sales floor stock).

patterns.

API OPERATIONS
Remember the following Uniform Contract:
Operation on Entities
Uniform API Operation
Description
Query Entities
GET Resource
GET must be used to
retrieve a representation of a
resource.
Create Entity
POST Resource
POST must be used to
create a new resource
Partial Update of an Entity
PATCH Resource
PATCH must be used to
partially update a resource
Remove an Entity
DELETE Resource
DELETE must be used to
remove a resource
Execute an Action on an
Entity
POST on TASK Resource
POST must be used to
execute Task Resources
Other Request Methods
POST on TASK Resource
GET and POST must not be
used to tunnel other request
methods.
Filtering and attribute selection rules are described in the TMF REST Design Guidelines.
Notifications are also described in a subsequent section.

API NOTIFICATIONS
For
every
single
of
operation
on
the
entities
use
the
following
templates
and
provide
sample REST notification POST calls.
It is assumed that the Pub/Sub uses the Register and UnRegister mechanisms described in
the REST Guidelines reproduced below.
images::image1.jpeg[]
Register listener
POST /hub
Description
Sets
the
communication
endpoint
address
the
service
instance
must
use
to
deliver
information about its health state, execution state, failures and metrics. Subsequent POST
calls will be rejected by the service if it does not support multiple listeners. In this case
DELETE /api/hub/{id} must be called before an endpoint can be created again.
Behavior
Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 204 if the request was successful.
Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 409 if request is not successful.
Usage Samples
Here’s an example of a request for registering a listener.
Request
POST /api/hub
Accept: application/json
{
 
"callback": "http://in.listener.com"
}
Response
201

Unregister listener
DELETE /hub/{id}
Description
Clears the communication endpoint address that was set by creating the Hub..
Behavior
Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 204 if the request was successful.
Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 404 if the resource is not found.
Usage Samples

Accept: application/json
